continuous_text.title: Here's My Classroom!
continuous_text.content:
Look! Here's my classroom.
And here are my friends!
Peter, Sarah, and Timothy,
Penny, Jack, and Jen!

Peter is cutting paper.
Penny is writing her name.
Sarah is listening to a story,
And Jack is playing a game.

Timothy is counting.
Jen is gluing.
We have fun and learn a lot.
What are your friends doing?

continuous_text.title: What's Maria Doing?
continuous_text.content:
Frame 1: What's Maria doing? She's cutting paper.
Frame 2: No, she isn't. She's using the computer.
Frame 3: No, she isn't. Look! Now Maria is writing on the board.
Frame 4: No! Look over here. Maria is gluing a picture.
Frame 5: How many Marias are there in our class? There's one Maria here.
Frame 6: And there's one Maria here. Yes, there are two Marias!

continuous_text.title: Math Homework
continuous_text.content:
1 There are eleven girls in the class and nineteen boys. There are thirty children in the class.
2 There are fourteen chairs in Classroom 1. The children move thirteen of them to Classroom 2. Now there are fifty chairs in Classroom 1.
3 The children have fifteen cupcakes. They eat four. Now they have twelve cupcakes.
4 There are eighteen pictures on the paper. Lucy cuts out sixteen pictures. Now there are two pictures on the paper.
5 There are a hundred children on the playground. Forty go into their classrooms. Now there are seventy children on the playground.
continuous_text.notes: Written as homework by student 'Katie Timms'

continuous_text.content:
Mrs. Green: It's hot in the classroom. Open the window, please, Lucy.
Lucy: OK.
Mrs. Green: Don't stand on the table. There's a computer on it! Be careful!
Lucy: Can I stand on the computer?
Mrs. Green: Don't be silly! Stand on the chair, open the window, and then sit down. And be quick, please, Lucy.

continuous_text.title: Classes, but Not in a Classroom!
continuous_text.content:
Are classes always in classrooms? No, they aren't!
These students in Turkey aren't in their classroom today. They're in a forest. They're studying trees and animals.
These students live in the mountains in France. They're having a P.E. class. It's very cold, but they're having fun. They love to ski.
These students in the United States are having a science class in the school garden. They're growing plants and flowers.
These students are studying English in a classroom in Bangladesh. Their school is a boat! Bangladesh is a wet country. Sometimes schools close, but this school is always open.

There are three crocodiles
Taking a bath.
They have thin mouths,
But big teeth!
Look out! Look out!

continuous_text.title: Come On and Play
continuous_text.content:
We're playing on the playground.
There are a lot of games to play.
Soccer, tennis, and volleyball.
What do you want to play today?

Paul likes playing on the swings.
Emma likes running and climbing.
We all love riding our bikes.
Tell us! What do you like doing?

We're playing on the playground.
It's always so much fun.
Come on and play with us.
We play with everyone!

continuous_text.title: We Like Playing Together!
continuous_text.content:
Frame 1: This is a nice playground! Yes, it is. What do you like doing on the playground?
Frame 2: I like playing soccer. My sister loves skateboarding.
Frame 3: What does your brother like doing? He loves playing volleyball.
Frame 4: We like playing together, too. How can you do that?
Frame 5: Just watch!
Frame 6: Wow! They're a great team. They like playing together.

continuous_text.title: Bones and Muscles
continuous_text.content:
a Playing is fun, and our bones and muscles help us play. Our bodies move when our muscles pull our bones into different positions.
b Our hands have a lot of bones. There are 27 bones in one hand. When we throw a ball with our hands, we use 34 muscles.
c Our feet have a lot of bones, too. There are 26 bones in one foot. When we kick a ball with our foot, we use 13 muscles. When we jump, we use more than 70 muscles.
d When we exercise every day, we use our muscles, and they grow strong. But when we don't exercise, they grow weak. Milk, yogurt, and cheese help make our bones strong. We need to take good care of our bones and muscles.

Anna: Does your sister like to play sports?
Ben: She doesn't like to play soccer or basketball, but she loves to skateboard.
Anna: Me, too! It's my favorite sport.
Ben: What about your brothers? What sports do they like?
Anna: They like volleyball and tennis, and they love to swim. But they don't like to swim in the ocean.
Ben: Me neither! It's very cold.

continuous_text.title: Games You Play
continuous_text.content:
1 I like to play jacks. I play on my own, but you can play with friends, too. You need a small ball and ten jacks. You throw the ball, and you pick up the jacks before you catch the ball again. (Elena, Guatemala)
2 Children in my city like to play marbles after school. A lot of people can play this game together. You hit a marble with your finger. When I win my friends' marbles, I'm very happy. (Arnav, India)
3 My friends and I like to play mancala. It's a game for two people. You need a board and some stones. You move the stones around the board. It's good when you catch your friend's stones. (John, Ghana)
